cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Hand It Over
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. Let me fix that cupboard hinge. The door's lower than when you started.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm just finding the right screw.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. You've tried four. Give me the screwdriver while you find it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll tell everyone you fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can announce the repair. I'll stand behind you with the screwdriver, keeping the door attached.

mechanism: A uses exact hinge-repair corrections to obtain the screwdriver and control of a task B is mishandling, then answers B credit concern without surrendering the takeover.
confusable: D25 would quietly transfer labour away from A; here A actively wants the work and tool because A judges B technique inadequate.
comparison: Seating alternative preserves B planning effort while changing control; hinge alternative offers public credit while A takes the physical repair.
seedUse: Drooping door, wrong screws and credit concern derive from D36-a; S03 gives specific alignment and handling corrections to justify takeover.
